learningObjectives: Select and justify log files in a business scenario.
Select and justify alerts in a business scenario.
reviewScope: Official topic comparison and original-question editorial review; not vendor endorsement.

elements.description: The PEGA log contains operational information, warnings and errors. ALERT contains threshold-based performance events; ALERTSECURITY contains security alerts. Additional logs depend on configured appenders, such as BIX extracts or security-event logging. Capture timestamp, node and requestor context before correlating evidence.

elements.text: Worked example: A failed connector at 14:10 has an exception in PEGA. A slow report around the same time has an ALERT event; correlate them rather than assuming all log types represent the same failure.

elements.description: An alert identifies a threshold or security event, not a fully established root cause. My Alerts focuses on session events by default; broader logs and PDC provide wider context. Use event frequency and affected interactions to prioritize investigation, while avoiding unnecessary sensitive data in diagnostics.

elements.text: Worked example: One slow operation among many requests and repeated slow operations for nearly every user need different priorities. Check the interaction and recurrence in PDC before choosing a fix.

elements.title: Training environment checklist
items: Implement the worked example in a training application; use synthetic data.
Test the expected path and at least one failure or boundary condition.
Explain why the alternative mechanism would not meet the requirement.
Revisit incorrect answers in Smart Review rather than memorizing option positions.

elements.text: These notes target the '25 exam. Shared Academy pages may show newer labels with '25 applicability; verify screens in your training environment.

examPitfalls.title: Alert versus cause
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Every threshold breach proves that the database is faulty.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Correlate timings and context before deciding the cause.

examPitfalls.title: Log scopes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: My Alerts always shows every session on every node.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Distinguish the session view from broader system logs.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer needs an application exception and operational warning. Which log is the starting point?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The PEGA/system log records operational information, warnings and errors.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A database operation exceeds a performance threshold. Which log contains the related performance alert?
practiceQuiz.rationale: ALERT records performance-related threshold events. BIX output serves an extraction-specific purpose.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which log is associated with security alert events?
practiceQuiz.rationale: ALERTSECURITY records security alerts. Other security event logs can also exist depending on configured appenders.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO help correlate a user's report with diagnostic logs?

options.text: The approximate timestamp and requestor/operator context
The affected node and interaction when available

practiceQuiz.rationale: Time, requestor, node and interaction narrow the relevant events and avoid mixing unrelated failures.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An alert threshold is exceeded once. What is the safe interpretation?

options.text: Investigate its context; the alert alone does not establish the root cause
Assume the application must be offline

practiceQuiz.rationale: Alerts flag conditions for investigation. Root-cause analysis requires context and related measurements.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: My Alerts initially shows which scope?

options.text: All events in all external systems automatically
The current session's alerts by default

practiceQuiz.rationale: The session-oriented default differs from broader system logs and monitoring aggregation.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which evidence helps prioritize two otherwise similar performance alerts?

options.text: The number of case stages regardless of impact
Recurrence rate and impact on the affected interaction
The length of the log filename alone

practiceQuiz.rationale: Frequency and user impact provide context for prioritization. A filename is not an impact measurement.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An exception message contains customer identifiers. What should diagnostic handling consider?

options.text: Copy all credentials into the message
Restrict access and avoid unnecessary sensitive data in logs
Publish all details in a public error banner
Ignore permissions because logs are technical

practiceQuiz.rationale: Diagnostics can expose sensitive information. Provide useful evidence with appropriate access and data minimization.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.
